sources.snippet: Sep 12, 2026 · What is the EU AI Act? The EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689) is the world's first comprehensive horizontal legal framework for artificial intelligence. It entered into force on 1 August 2024 and applies progressively across four risk tiers. The Act uses a risk-based approach: the higher the potential harm, the stricter the obligations.

sources.snippet: THE EU AI ACT OVERVIEW OF KEY RULES AND REQUIREMENTS On 12 July 2024, the EU Artificial Intelligence Act (AI Act) was finally published in the EU’s Official Journal1, marking the conclusion of a long elaboration and adoption process.

answer: The EU AI Act entered into force on 1 August 2024 [5]. Prohibited AI practices became applicable on 2 February 2025 [1]. AI literacy provisions also became applicable on that date [1]. Governance rules and general-purpose AI model obligations applied from 2 August 2025 [4]. Article 50 transparency rules and innovation measures apply from 2 August 2026 [1]. Enforcement by the AI Office and national authorities also started on 2 August 2026 [4]. High-risk systems listed in Annex III face obligations from 2 December 2027 [2]. High-risk systems embedded in regulated products face obligations from 2 August 2028 [2]. The Act fully rolls out by 2 August 2028 [1]. The AI Omnibus amendments entered into force on 27 July 2026 [4]. A ban on AI systems generating non-consensual intimate imagery takes effect in December 2026 [5].
